comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Done for its purpose: everything the Rust port needs is now data. 9 files, 73 cases, all claimed by a driver and counted by the gate.

Extracted (44 Swift tests -> 73 cases): keymap, composition-arbiter, agent-state, control-stream-message, frame-decoder, socket-discovery, key-encoder, log-record, pane-input.

Two format decisions worth knowing before adding more:
- Sequential concepts get a trace: a case is a list of steps and the expectation is the ordered trace of what went out, tagged by channel. frame-decoder and pane-input use it.
- Fakes are part of the contract. pane-input names what its test encoder does, because a Rust fake that spelled a keystroke differently would make every case disagree for a reason unrelated to the behavior.

Deliberately left native, and why:
- SurfaceView (5): drives AppKit with synthesized NSEvents.
- KeyTranslation (7): the hybrid case - macOS driver, portable KeyEvent expectation. Worth doing when a second shell exists; does not block the port.
- Log sink concurrency, unwritable path, monotonic clock (4): properties of an implementation, not behaviors.
- Control-stream socket delivery (1): framing across a real socket and losing the accept race.
- Grid fidelity and the key-encoder survey (8): already snapshot-driven, oracle is libghostty upstream. a_27Haa38Gp covers moving the survey's keystroke list into data.
- MusterPerf comparison (10): tests the harness, not the core.

Verified the mechanism by breaking it four ways: wrong expectation prints a readable diff with the why, a blank why refuses to load, a misspelled modifier reports that the case was never evaluated rather than that behavior failed, and an unclaimed corpus file fails the lint.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Turn the core's tests into data plus a thin driver, before any porting starts. The order matters: cases extracted from a passing implementation are proven, and become the port's acceptance criterion instead of something written afterward to match whatever Rust happened to do.

Classified over the 81 tests as they stand:
- ~51 are pure f(input) -> output and become case tables: agent states, composition arbiter, keymap resolution, control-stream messages, frame decoding, socket discovery, pane command, key encoding, perf comparison, log record encoding.
- ~16 are sequential and become scenario/trace files: input routing (a sequence of sends -> an ordered trace of channel and intent), grid fidelity (already snapshot-driven).
- ~7 stay native and should: SurfaceView driving AppKit with synthesized NSEvents, log sink concurrency.
- 7 are hybrid: NSEvent -> KeyEvent translation keeps a Swift driver but a portable expectation, so a GTK shell writes its own table producing the same KeyEvent.

Doctrine and the three failure modes it has to answer are in docs/testing.md, 'The conformance corpus'. In short: every case carries a required non-empty 'why' or the driver fails it; every file declares source as recorded/ported/authored; disagreement between implementations is never resolved by editing the corpus; and the gate checks that every corpus file is claimed by a driver and that no driver ran zero cases.

Done when ./dev is still green with the Swift tests reading from the corpus, and the case count is reported rather than assumed.
title: Extract the conformance corpus, while the Swift suite is green
